draft.title: Newton's laws of motion
card: First law
A body stays still or keeps moving at a steady speed in a straight line unless an unbalanced force acts on it. This resistance to a change in motion is called inertia.
Second law
Acceleration is in proportion to the net force and happens in the direction of that force. For the same force, a body with more mass accelerates less. F = m × a.
Third law
When one body applies a force to another, the second body applies an equal force back in the opposite direction. The two forces act on different bodies.
A heavier body has more inertia, so it takes more force to start it, stop it or change its direction.
draft.remember: No net force, no change in motion. More force means more acceleration. Every force has an equal and opposite reaction.

a.q: A netballer and a rugby forward are each pushed with the same net force from rest. The forward has more mass. What happens?
opts: The netballer accelerates more than the forward
The forward accelerates more than the netballer
Both accelerate by the same amount
The forward does not accelerate at all
a.why: With the same net force, acceleration is smaller for the body with more mass (a = F ÷ m). The forward has more inertia, so the netballer accelerates more. The forward still accelerates, because the net force is not zero.
a.clue: Same force, different mass: who changes speed more easily?

b.q: A swimmer pushes backwards on the water with her hands and feet and moves forwards. Which law best explains this, and why?
opts: Third law: the water pushes back on her with equal force
First law: she keeps moving until a force stops her
Second law: her mass decides how far the water moves
Third law: her push on the water moves her forwards
b.why: The swimmer pushes on the water, and the water pushes back on her with an equal and opposite force. That reaction force acts on her, so it moves her forwards. The last option is tempting, but her push acts on the water, not on her.
b.clue: Which body does the reaction force act on?

a.best: The netballer accelerates more than the forward

b.best: Third law: the water pushes back on her with equal force

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the right option the 'last option' and says it is tempting but wrong. The options are shuffled, and in this order the last option is the intended right answer ('the water pushes back on her with equal force'). The why should name the distractor by its content: 'her push on the water moves her forwards'.
